An earlier note in this file assumed the list might be metadata-only and that editing off a list row could PUT an empty workflow over a saved one; that specific data-loss premise is now DISPROVEN. The Modify flow still calls viewWorkflow first (see useWorkflows.loadWorkflowForEdit) because it is the canonical single-record read and it refuses to open the builder if `workflow` is absent — a cheap guard, not a fix for a confirmed bug.

Root cause of the reported 404 on GET /api/decision/get_workflow_list: DECISION_TEMPLATE had NO entry in backends.js BACKEND_PATHS (bare host, no gateway prefix), and the route file (src/app/api/decision/[...path]/route.js) hardcoded a hand-guessed prefix '/p1_decisionmodel/decisionworkflow' (all-lowercase, underscore-joined) with snake_case leaf names (get_workflow_list, template_option_list, config_workflow). The real backend, confirmed via live openapi.json, mounts at the decisionops-pod2 gateway under the SLASH-separated, camelCase segment '/p1/decisionModel/decisionworkflow/*' with camelCase leaf op names (getWorkflowList, templateOptionList, configWorkflow). Same bug class previously seen on SYMBOLIC_AI/PLANT_GPT (missing gateway prefix) — this time compounded by wrong casing/segmentation on top.

Right-clicking an equipment node on the home diagram opens a ContextMenu with 'Configure <label>' and navigates to /asset-config/<label>, a full page that runs the exact same three endpoints. What DID move is the UI layer, which was previously locked inside the admin route folder: useAssetConfig -> src/hooks/asset-config/useAssetConfig.js, ConfigFieldRenderer + CheckboxDropdown -> src/components/config-fields/, plus a new shared src/components/asset-config/AssetConfigForm.jsx (variant='flat' for the modal, 'cards' for the page). getCurrentUsername moved to src/lib/currentUser.js (workflowUtils.js re-exports it) so the shared hook doesn't import out of a route folder. 2026-08-03 BUG FOUND & FIXED — assetConfigOption's response was being parsed against the WRONG shape, and the fix was driven by a real browser capture the user pasted, not by the contract table. The code read `features.config` unconditionally (`optionResult?.data?.features?.config ?? optionResult?.features?.config ?? {}`), which is shape (B), the CONFIGURED-asset shape from the 2026-07-28 doc sample. The live response for an UNCONFIGURED asset is shape (A): the groups sit directly on `features` and there is no `config` key at all. Result: `config` resolved to `{}` on every unconfigured asset, so the form silently rendered 'No configurable fields returned for this asset' instead of the template-selection dropdown — i.e. the primary path (configure a brand-new asset) never worked. Now handled by extractConfigGroups(), which detects both shapes. SECOND defect in the same code path: each group's backend-supplied `name` and `description` were being thrown away and the section heading was rendered from a humanized version of the group KEY. The backend's own copy is what the reference UI shows ('template Selection' / 'Select a template to configure the asset' — note the deliberate lowercase 't', which a humanizer would have destroyed), so the whole group object is now kept intact through state and `group.name` wins, with humanizeGroupKey only as the fallback. Keeping the group whole also means save() echoes name/description back inside `data`, matching assetConfig's documented contract ('the filled config schema returned by assetConfigOption') rather than sending a stripped-down subset — UNVERIFIED against a live save, so if the backend ever rejects the extra keys, that is the first thing to check.

2026-08-03 asset_id SOURCE on the /home entry point: the equipment node's `data.label`. This is not a preference — it's the only candidate the CPCP diagram contract offers. GET /loadDiagram's live-verified node shape (api-data/cpcp-configuration.json) is `{ id: 'node_1', data: { label: 'Pump 1', componentType: 'api_p' } }`: `id` is a synthetic per-diagram key, `componentType` is a drawing/catalog key, and `data.code` (present on catalog components) is raw SVG/TSX markup, not an asset code. There is NO asset_id field anywhere in the diagram contract. OPEN RISK, flagged rather than worked around: node labels are inline-editable on the workflow-diagram canvas (EquipmentNode.jsx), so a user renaming a node silently changes the asset_id this flow sends. If the backend needs a stable asset key, the diagram contract has to carry one — do not paper over this client-side by deriving an id from componentType.
